key_insight: LongStraw enables million-token RL post-training under a fixed GPU budget by reusing prompt computation, keeping only necessary model state, and replaying response branches to control memory.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical execution stack for long-context agent training when inference contexts are already very long but RL post-training must stay within limited GPU memory.
method: Evaluates the shared prompt without autograd
Retains only model-specific state needed for later tokens
Replays short response branches one at a time to shrink the live training graph
evidence_signal: On 8 H20 GPUs, it reaches 2.1M-token positions for grouped Qwen scoring/backward with only 0.21 GB extra peak memory at larger group size, and a stress test reaches 4.46M positions.
watch_item: The reported results validate execution capacity, not full training correctness, because the prompt state is detached and some distributed forward/gradient composition paths are still incomplete.
paper_title: LongStraw: Long-Context RL Beyond 2M Tokens under a Fixed GPU Budget
